reasons: Governing law in Section 18.3 is the laws of the State of New York (conflicts excluded), which is exactly the playbook's preferred choice, and the deterministic check confirms the jurisdiction is within the accepted set.
The finding is claimed compliant with no redline and no counterparty comment, which is the expected output for a compliant status; nothing actionable is being wrongly proposed.

The rationale accurately reads the forum mechanic: Article XVII escalates to Senior Executives (45 days), then expert determination for specified matters, then ICC arbitration with the seat in New York if Ono demands and Osaka if Array demands. Since we are Ono (Osaka, Japan), neither branch imposes a hostile foreign seat, and the respondent-forum split is not adverse to us; the walk-away trigger (counterparty home venue / mandatory arbitration seated abroad relative to us) is absent.

Arbitration in lieu of New York County courts is a departure from the preferred wording, but the rationale correctly notes it for the file rather than redlining, consistent with the instruction not to flag terms that benefit our party and to note sub-elements short of preferred in the rationale; the interim-relief court carve-out in 17.3(g) further mitigates.
Rationale is factually consistent with the quoted paragraphs and definitions (ICC Rules, three-arbitrator panel, seat allocation, 45-day escalation); no misstatements identified.
